response.sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALP) AS avg_alp, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_hct FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory a WHERE a.ID = p.ID AND a.`U-PRO` = '-') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory b WHERE b.ID = p.ID AND b.RA = '-') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY avg_hct IS NULL, avg_hct DESC, p.ID LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: '-' is matched as an exact string; no trimming or variant dash characters are considered.
The two '-' conditions may be met by different Laboratory rows, each checked with its own EXISTS.
AVG(ALP) and AVG(HCT) use all Laboratory rows for the patient, not only the rows that met the '-' conditions, with NULLs ignored and no rounding.
Only patients present in the Patient table are listed, and patients with a NULL SEX are kept as their own group.
Ties in average HCT are broken by ID ascending, which the request does not specify.
